posts.body_html:
Had the chance to visit Rob's greenhouse this past weekend, and of course, his crops look amazing! While I'm uploading some photos, here's a few homies that I was able to meet up with:


From L to R:Drew Martinez (of Carnivero), Rod Quebral(talented Southern California grower),and Rob Co of the Pitcher Plant Project:




Here's Rob(to the left) and Rod(to the right) trying to look tough, but you know how it is with us Sarracenia growers....it's unnatural for us to be thugs. Calen is one of the few that has the talent to look gangsta on call, but that's another story:


Crops overview with my wife and Ellie in the background (it was father's day, so I dragged the whole family! They actually loved it):







That's a nice lid you got there, pal:



The famous LW x Adrian Slack, this is a seedling (not legacy):


neat hybrid, almost looks like hummer's hammerhead was in this mix:



Not sure there's enough seedlings here, Rob might want to grow a few more:



What's insane is how a dead Drosophyllum lucitanicum stem looks exactly like a dead cactus stem:



Here's the drosophyllum that I gave Rob, it looks better than mine!





The Icky, Icky, STICKY Green....drosophyllum:


The highland house-notice the helis and nepenthes:



Freakin amazing: a neighbor was dumping this sink away, and Rob turned it into this:


"Cool"ulent collection...cuz they don't suck:





An adrian slack hybrid, almost an adrian slack imposter-looking plant:



This is a seed grown oreophila originally from private property in Alabama. There's some speculation that it might be hybridized with something else, but in my opinion, it looks as pure as can be! Check out the colors on this clone, pretty darn amazing:


Reptilian Rose hybrid, looks Adrian Slacky:




Rob's recessive gene project:



An amazing Travis Wyman hybrid involving reptilian rose:


Love the color on this thing:



Some red throated oreos from Jerry's place:


minor giant:


Some more minors:



Here's that oreophila imposter, you can see flava mixed in:



In contrast, a real oreophila, with an amazing red throat:


Another reptilian rose hybrid:


S. flava var. atropurpurea(Carolina Clone):


More pics to come!
